records.name: Lee et al. (2008): monolayer graphene in-plane stiffness (2D)

uncertainty.interpretation: The paper reports a ± value; its statistical type and coverage have not been verified. Do not treat it as a confidence interval, standard deviation, standard error or certified bound.

method.inference: Two-dimensional in-plane elastic stiffness inferred by fitting AFM force–displacement curves with a membrane indentation model; this is a model-dependent experimental summary.
model_assumptions: Clamped isotropic circular membrane under central indentation; the elastic fit uses the point-load approximation in Eq. (2).
Negligible bending stiffness.
Poisson ratio 0.165 is a modeling assumption, not a measured result.

notes: These are stiffness-fit statistics only, not breaking-test sample counts.
The distribution standard deviation 30 N/m is distinct from the reported stiffness uncertainty ±50 N/m; neither statistic is replaced by the other.

gaps: Supporting supplementary material was inaccessible; uncertainty type and coverage have not been verified.
Temperature, atmosphere, humidity and loading rate have not been verified.
No raw-data reanalysis, independent replication, specimen-condition validation or independent scientific review is claimed.

evidence.locator: Science 321 (2008), p. 387 final paragraph (340 ± 50 N/m); p. 386 final paragraph (23 membranes from 2 flakes); p. 387 opening and Fig. 3A discussion (67 fits; mean 342 N/m, standard deviation 30 N/m); p. 386 Eqs. (1)–(2) and membrane-model discussion; p. 385 and Fig. 1 (preparation, monolayer identification and spans).
evidence.verified_as: Reported two-dimensional elastic stiffness and separate fit-distribution statistics; a model-dependent observation rather than a universal elastic bound.

limits: Observational context from one study, not a theoretical or universal material limit, engineering allowable or new executable rule.
This two-dimensional force-per-length quantity must not be identified with a three-dimensional pressure merely by changing unit labels. No thickness conversion is performed.
Matching N/m units do not make in-plane stiffness and breaking strength the same quantity. Material state, dimensionality, quantity, method and stress/strain conventions must also be compatible.
These two records share one study and are not independent confirmations. They cannot be passed to the composite evaluator or overlaid on its volume-fraction sweeps.

The authors infer defect-free behavior in the highly stressed region beneath the tip; this is not independent imaging proof for every entire membrane or a guarantee for macroscopic or processed graphene.

records.name: Lee et al. (2008): monolayer graphene breaking strength (2D)

uncertainty.interpretation: The paper reports a ± value; its statistical type and coverage have not been verified. Do not treat it as a confidence interval, standard deviation, standard error or certified bound.

method.inference: Two-dimensional breaking strength inferred from AFM failure measurements using nonlinear membrane elasticity and finite-element simulation. The constitutive convention is sigma=E2D*epsilon+D2D*epsilon^2 with second Piola–Kirchhoff stress and uniaxial Lagrangian strain; its model maximum is -E2D^2/(4*D2D). These are source-model descriptions, not executable formulas or direct uniform-stress measurements.
model_assumptions: Clamped isotropic circular membrane indented centrally by a finite-radius AFM tip; the failure inference uses nonlinear finite-element modeling and accounts for tip radius, not the point-load approximation used for elastic fitting.
Negligible bending stiffness.
Poisson ratio 0.165 is a modeling assumption, not a measured result.

gaps: Supporting supplementary material was inaccessible; uncertainty type and coverage have not been verified.
Temperature, atmosphere, humidity and loading rate have not been verified.
No raw-data reanalysis, independent replication, specimen-condition validation or independent scientific review is claimed.
Breaking-test sample counts are not verified in this record; the stiffness-fit counts are not transferred to breaking strength.

evidence.locator: Science 321 (2008), p. 388 opening paragraph (42 ± 4 N/m); p. 387 final-column numerical-simulation paragraph (nonlinear finite-element failure inference and tip-radius dependence); p. 386 Eq. (1) and associated nonlinear constitutive and maximum-stress discussion; p. 385 and Fig. 1 (preparation, monolayer identification and spans).
evidence.verified_as: Source-reported model-inferred two-dimensional breaking strength from AFM failure, with the source stress/strain convention retained; not a directly measured uniform tensile stress or universal bound.

limits: Observational context from one study, not a theoretical or universal material limit, engineering allowable or new executable rule.
This two-dimensional force-per-length quantity must not be identified with a three-dimensional pressure merely by changing unit labels. No thickness conversion is performed.
Matching N/m units do not make in-plane stiffness and breaking strength the same quantity. Material state, dimensionality, quantity, method and stress/strain conventions must also be compatible.
These two records share one study and are not independent confirmations. They cannot be passed to the composite evaluator or overlaid on its volume-fraction sweeps.

Breaking strength here depends on the nonlinear constitutive inference and reference stress/strain measures; do not substitute Cauchy stress, engineering stress or a generic three-dimensional tensile strength.

The authors infer defect-free behavior in the highly stressed region beneath the tip; this is not independent imaging proof for every entire membrane or a guarantee for macroscopic or processed graphene.

material.name: Freestanding monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)
material.preparation_notes: Naturally occurring bulk MoS2/molybdenite; PMMA/PVA-assisted transfer to patterned SiO2. Polymer-removal anneal: vacuum, 400 °C, 4 h. This is preparation, not test temperature or atmosphere.

method.calibration: Cantilever spring constants calibrated using the thermal method; PDF p. 6 (F), Materials and Methods.
method.poissons_ratio_role: Bulk MoS2 value adopted for the membrane model; not measured for these monolayers.
method.stress_strain_measure_status: The inspected main text does not explicitly identify Cauchy/engineering/second-Piola stress or engineering/Lagrangian strain conventions. Do not inherit the Lee graphene conventions.

q_source_report.audit_arithmetic_status: Curator arithmetic check of the printed formula at printed ν, not a source-reported measurement or a replacement q.
q_source_report.curation_action: Retain all printed inputs separately and flag discrepancy; do not select a corrected fit constant, refit curves, alter E2D, or recompute strength.
q_source_report.fit_constant_status: The inspected PDF does not establish whether the printed formula, stated q, or another value was actually used in the least-squares fits.

method.inference: Least-squares inference of E2D and pretension from AFM force–deflection curves using the circular-membrane force law, not direct uniform tensile-modulus measurement.
model_assumptions: Clamped circular, prestretched, isotropic membrane; linear material constitutive assumption.
Eq. (1): F = σ0^(2D) πδ + E^(2D) q^3 δ^3/r^2. The linear term describes pretension and the cubic term membrane stretching; bending-dominated plate behavior is not the fitted regime.
Point-loading approximation is used for the fit; the source states r_tip/r approximately 0.05.
Printed q inconsistency is retained separately in q_source_report.

loading_rate.locator: PDF p. 2 (B), right column, cantilever-deflection/loading paragraph

notes: Probe translation speed is not membrane strain rate or force/stress rate.
An air temperature controller is reported to reduce drift; no numerical test temperature, controlled gas composition, pressure or humidity is reported in the inspected main text.
Do not use the 400 °C vacuum processing step as the indentation test condition.

sample_metadata.locator: PDF p. 3 (C), left column, first body paragraph; stiffness average n=9 additionally PDF p. 4 (D), right column.
notes: Multiple indentation curves were acquired per hole; the total number of curves is not supplied.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 4 (D), right column, least-squares-fit paragraph and immediately following uncertainty sentence; also PDF p. 1 (A), Abstract and publisher abstract.
evidence.verified_as: Exact text-reported 2D property average and reported standard deviation, with source-model assumptions retained.

limits: A model-dependent summary from one study; not a theoretical or universal bound, engineering allowable, executable rule, or new independent replication.
Canonical 2D quantity in N/m. No conversion to Pa/GPa and no assigned default thickness.
Equal N/m units do not make stiffness and breaking strength the same quantity.

material.preparation: Scotch-tape mechanical exfoliation from high-quality hBN single crystals onto prepatterned SiO2/Si

defect_status.source_description: high-quality single-crystalline mono- and few-layer BN

tip_radii.measurement: Transmission electron microscopy, as reported by authors
tip_radii.locator: Methods > Materials and fabrication; Figure S4 shows 12.6 nm diameter for one tip

method.calibration: Cantilever spring constants determined using combined thermal-noise and Sader methods

effective_thickness_convention.role: Source-used layer thickness for volumetric conversion and finite-element geometry; not the AFM apparent height and not a curator default conversion.
effective_thickness_convention.selected_2d_values_status: Both selected N/m summaries are expressly printed in source; neither is generated by the curator.

method.inference: Fit the loading response with source Eq. 2 to infer E2D and pretension; not a direct uniform tensile-modulus measurement.

fit_force_law.source_locator: Results > Mechanical tests by indentation, Eq. 2 and following paragraph

q_source_report.fit_constant_status: The article prescribes the formula and ν; raw fit implementation not inspected.
